label: Three-pass method
summary: The three-pass method is a structured reading and extraction workflow that combines thematic analysis with TAO topic mapping. It runs in a zoom-out / zoom-in / zoom-out rhythm: a wide thematic read first, then close entity and relationship extraction, then a final coherence check against the original argument. It is the structural backbone of the Thematic TAO method.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike developed the three-pass method to resolve a tension she hit when building the concept graph for her garden: thematic analysis surfaces emergent themes but lacks consistent structure, while TAO extraction gives typed triples but can technically misrepresent what a post actually argues if done without a prior gestalt read. She now uses the method to drive the /auto-tag process, which enriches garden posts and updates the concept graph by treating each post as an occurrence of the topics it discusses and the associations it contributes.
open_questions: The post notes the graph 'grows better' but the sentence is unfinished — it's unclear what the intended claim about graph quality actually is.

The method is described as still being developed, so it's an open question whether the coherence check pass is sufficient to catch all cases where extracted triples reconstruct a different argument than the one the text makes.
